record.paper_title: Open problems of the 33rd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: Let G be a graph that is a disjoint union of cycles, and let H be a graph that is a disjoint union of copies of K_4. Must the union G ∪ H be 4-colorable?

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.1 Let G be a disjoint union of cycles. Let H be a disjoint union of K4's. Is
G ∪ H 4-colourable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a graph each of whose connected components is a cycle (so $G$ is a vertex-disjoint union of cycles). Let $H$ be a graph each of whose connected components is a complete graph on $4$ vertices (so $H$ is a vertex-disjoint union of copies of $K_4$). Assume $G$ and $H$ share the same vertex set, and let $G \cup H$ denote the graph on this common vertex set whose edge set is the union of the edge sets of $G$ and $H$. 

Determine whether, for every such pair $(G,H)$, the graph $G \cup H$ admits a proper vertex colouring with at most $4$ colours.
artifact.status_search_result: The "cycles plus K_4's" problem is a well-known special case of the Strong Colouring Conjecture and remains open. A 2024 preprint reduces it to a specific 3-colourability question, and only partial cases are known (e.g., when H has at most one odd component longer than a triangle, or at most three triangles in related variants). No full solution has been reported.

status_evidence.title: A reduction of the "cycles plus K_4's" problem
status_evidence.snippet: Reduces the open 'cycles plus K_4's' 4-colourability question to a specific 3-colourability problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is treated as open and only reduced, not solved.
